Lamborghini Aventador SV Thinks Its Fast, Gets Its V12 Handed Over on a Plate by 10-Sec Audi Diesel
30 photos
Photo: YouTube/OFFICIALLY GASSED - OG
Picture a civilized Sunday family dinner where prim German engineers pass the transmission oil to flamboyant Italian stylists, a domestic arrangement forged in 1998 when Audi asked (and received) the maid Lamborghini into marriage.
That union followed three major directions of shared lineage: ten-cylinder mid-engine supercar architectures, modular sport-utility platforms underpinning the Urus, and reliable German electronics that stopped Italian dashboards from spontaneously combusting. Yet Lamborghini never followed Audi down its darkest rabbit hole: coal-rolling diesel power. While Sant'Agata Bolognese spent decades worshipping high-revving gasoline aristocracy, Ingolstadt dug a soot-stained tunnel straight into compression-ignition madness, conquering endurance racing with oil-burning prototypes.
However, do not confuse what Audi did on the race tracks with what it is sensible for everyday commuting. Until recently, diesel remained the go-to energy source for long-driving, budget-saving means of transportation (trains, ships, trucks, vans, or tiny city cars). Then backyard tuners scrapped the “sensible” part, setting the stage for Jamie Sonuga on the Officially Gassed OG channel to commit the most delicious drag-racing heresy.
Photo: YouTube/OFFICIALLY GASSED - OG In the aristocratic Italian corner sits a white Lamborghini Aventador SV Roadster, an exotic masterpiece valued at over £600,000 (some $800k). Its mid-mounted, naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V12 engine retains factory calibration, screaming out 750 bhp, alongside 680 Nm of torque (502 lb-ft). Weighing 1.6 tons, it packs a hefty 455 bhp per ton, all-wheel drive, seven-speed ISR shifting, and Pirelli P Zero Corsa tires.
Challenging that Italian royalty is a humble 2012 Audi A5 Coupé that originally left Ingolstadt as a sensible commuter car. In standard factory specification, a 2012 Audi A5 3.0 TDI Quattro Coupé carried a 3.0-liter V6 diesel producing 242 bhp and 500 Nm of torque (369 lb-ft), weighing 1.7 tons with 141 bhp per ton, hitting 60 mph in 5.6 seconds, topping out at 155 mph, and returning 49.6 mpg combined.
Enter Audrius from APA Performance, who bought this 2012 Audi A5 for £2,900 (around $3,900) and injected £30,000 (some $40,300) of pure mechanical lunacy into it. He swapped in a fully built 3.0-liter BiTDI DEHA twin-turbocharged V6 diesel that originally produced 309 bhp and 650 Nm (480 lb-ft) from the factory, adding custom engine and AFR gearbox calibrations, plus a Cloudvag second-gear launch solution to unleash 715 bhp, 1,300 Nm (960 lb-ft), and 397 bhp per ton.
Routing almost twice the Lamborghini's twist through an eight-speed ZF automatic transmission and all-wheel drive to Continental SportContact 7 tires, this daily-driven coupe arrived ready for war. Jamie Sonuga outlined a simple battle plan: two solo quarter-mile runs each, then best-of-three standing drag and roll races.
Photo: YouTube/OFFICIALLY GASSED - OG During the pre-race rev battle, the Lamborghini shrieked operatically while the Audi coughed out an apocalyptic pyroclastic cloud of sun-eclipsing black soot. However, since the race in England, there was no sun on the sky, leaving only an ode to Greta to be heard from the stove pipes out the back of the Audi.
When Audrius staged for his solo quarter-mile runs, the comedy turned into a horror movie for Italian supercar owners everywhere. Despite cold tarmac, the grey coupe hooked up without spinning a wheel, laying down an opening pass of 10.64 seconds at 131 mph. With warm rubber on the second attempt, the diesel monster blasted through the quarter-mile in 10.56 seconds at 131 mph, leaving Jamie visibly worried behind the wheel of the Lambo.
Having guesstimated a 10.7-second pass while knowing the Audi once ran 10.3 seconds, Jamie asked Audrius if he could beat the borrowed supercar, and the builder deadpanned that the drag race would be easy. Climbing into the Lamborghini, Jamie engaged launch control on cold tires, hopping violently to 60 mph in 2.89 seconds for a 10.75-second pass before improving next run to 10.72 seconds at 132 mph.
Photo: YouTube/OFFICIALLY GASSED - OG Mathematics delivered a brutal verdict: on paper, a diesel coupe costing £32,900 all-in was 0.16 seconds quicker than a £600,000 Italian icon, separated by just 1 mph in trap speed. When the flag dropped for the first head-to-head drag race, the Lamborghini squirmed on cold tires while the Audi vanished behind a thick black smokescreen, holding its early lead to win by what Audrius gleefully called several full train lengths.
Faced with the dreadful possibility of losing two-nil to a glorified taxi, Jamie warmed his sticky Pirelli tires and prayed for Italian redemption in the second drag race. Both cars launched hard, yet the torque-rich Audi once again rocketed out front and stabilized its advantage down the runway. Feeling invincible, Audrius casually lifted one hand off the steering wheel to wave goodbye at the trailing Lamborghini, and his car immediately grenaded.
You’ve never seen instant karma at a more instantaneous instance than in this race. Comedic timing rarely achieves such theatrical perfection , as the Audi's black soot instantly transformed into a dense white fog bank the exact millisecond Audrius waved and grinned at his disheartened opponent. While the wounded coupe coasted and allowed the Lamborghini to tie the series at one-all, the pit diagnosis proved even funnier.
Photo: YouTube/OFFICIALLY GASSED - OG After rolling at walking speed over the finish line, Audrius’s wounded car came to a halt, and he then blipped the throttle of his still-running engine, and the exhaust pipe literally spat a shredded turbocharger impeller and a puddle of oil outside.
Inspecting the mangled metal turbine wheel resting on the tarmac, Jamie declared it the easiest blown-turbo diagnosis in history, prematurely ending the tiebreaker and roll races. The naysayers will probably argue that the Audi bit off more than it could chew. Please note one this: that turbo was installed on the engine since day one, one and a half years ago, and has endured sustained boosts of 3.6 bar (52 PSI!).
It has since clocked some 5,000 miles (8k km or thereabout) and 500 quarter-miler passes. In Audrius’ own words, that impeller had just about enough. Even more, the mechanic fixed his car the very next day, and is ready to battle any Lambo again (but maybe ones that less slow than this Aventador SV).

US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth delivers an address during the 23rd Shangri-La Dialogue summit in Singapore on May 30, 2026. (Photo by JAM STA ROSA / AFP via Getty Images)
WASHINGTON — Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth came out swinging against a potential impeachment today, dismissing the charges introduced in the House yesterday as simple “policy disagreements.”
“What one disgruntled and defeated congressman is attempting is not oversight, and it’s not accountability,” Hegseth told reporters at the Pentagon this morning. “It’s a political spectacle, a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment.”
Hegseth’s comments — the first time he has appeared before press at the Pentagon in over 180 days — come less than 24 hours after Kentucky Republican Rep. Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment against him. Massie, who lost his primary in May to a candidate backed by President Donald Trump, has been an outspoken critic of the administration, and especially Hegseth, over an array of issues.
In the 34-page resolution [ pdf ] filed Monday, Massie charged the defense secretary with committing “high crimes and misdemeanors” and called him “a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office.”
Specifically, Massie cited eight articles for impeachment centering on:
Violations of the War Powers Resolution of 1973 related to military operations against Iran;
Ignoring laws that minimize civilian casualties citing the US military strike on the Iranian elementary school that killed or injured more than 200 civilians;
Suppressing free speech for retaliating on Sen Mark Kelly, a retired Navy captain, for appearing in a video advising service members of their duty to disobey unlawful orders;
The kidnapping of a sovereign foreign leader associated with the abduction of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro,
Conducting an “unlawful” war in Yemen; and
Extrajudicial killings tied to the strikes on alleged drug boats in the Caribbean and Pacific waters.
“By subjecting persons merely suspected of criminal conduct to lethal military force without judicial process, without congressional authorization, and without establishing a lawful basis for treating such persons or vessels as military targets, Secretary Hegseth arrogated to himself and the Executive Branch the roles of judge, jury, and executioner and asserted a unilateral power to determine who may live and who may die,” the resolution said on the extrajudicial killings article of impeachment. Hegseth defended military operations under his watch, calling them “lawful” and “successful.”
“I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow,” he said during Tuesday’s briefing.
The House could vote on those articles of impeachment later this week and, if approved by a simple majority, it could be sent to the Senate for a trial under the current GOP leadership or next year when Democrats take control.
The House has only impeached two cabinet secretaries: Secretary of War William Belknap in 1876 and Secretary of Homeland Security Alejandro Mayorkas in 2024. (Though Hegseth refers to himself as the Secretary of War, his official title remains Secretary of Defense.)
This is not Massie’s first call to impeach Hegseth. In September, he announced plans to force a vote in the House to impeach Hegseth and had been waiting for Congress to return after the mid-term elections to again push the issue.
As Republicans suffered a historic midterm defeat and the prospect of Massie pushing the impeachment came, news reports emerged suggesting Hegseth’s job could be in jeopardy. At the time Trump told reporters he was not considering replacing Hegseth, but suggested Hegseth would be “very popular” if he became a Senator and took over Sen. Marsha Blackburn’s office when she moved into the Tennessee governor’s mansion.
But later in the week, reports began emerging that Blackburn was not considering appointing Hegseth to her vacant Senate seat.
Around the same time, the Pentagon’s official social media account kicked into high gear to defend Hegseth. It first released a five-plus minute a video of Hegseth standing outside the Pentagon defending the Iran war and denouncing the “sham articles of impeachment.”
“Their policies don’t work, so their obsession with political theater disguised as power drives them to try to destroy their opponents,” he said on the video posted on X. “It’s all about the politics of personal destruction. Didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me.”
This is a developing story and will be updated.

He Bought a Tesla Model X Plaid in March, Already Got Rid of It and Will Buy a Ford F-150 Lightning
28 photos
Photo: Cars and Bids
The owner of this Tesla Model X Plaid bought the six-seater EV back in March 2026. Eight months later, he listed it for sale and sold it in the blink of an eye. Why did he get rid of it so fast? He realized he is a truck guy after all.
The Tesla Model X inventory is sold out, so the only way to get your hands on one is the used car market. It looks like some people were really late to the party and realized they wanted it long after Tesla halted production. Now, they are willing to pay anything for it, even new Tesla Model X Plaid money for a pre-owned vehicle.
A longtime EV enthusiast, already at his fourth Tesla, the seller is being transparent about his Model X experience. He admits he enjoyed the performance, the technology, and the driving, but he is now going back to a Ford F-150 Lightning. "Being 6’5", I've really missed the legroom and spaciousness of the Lightning."
He realized he is a truck guy who enjoys doing truck stuff after all. That’s one thing you’d better not do in a Tesla, unless it’s the Cybertruck, but that one also has its days numbered. Tesla is winding down production by mid-2027 after it already pulled the plug on the Model X and the Model S to focus its resources on AI and robotics. There goes the auto industry…
Photo: Cars and Bids Finished in Stealth Grey over a black interior, it rides on 20-inch Perihelix wheels and sits on Tesla’s air suspension. The Falcon Wing rear doors spring upward to reveal a cabin in synthetic leather, hosting the six-seat configuration, a 17-inch horizontal center touchscreen, and a Yoke steering wheel .
It has the Full-Self Driving Capability, which is transferable, and the Luxe Package, which is not. Introduced back in August 2025 with a $10,000 baseline price increase for Tesla’s flagship models, the package was designed to transform the lineup into a fully loaded, worry-free luxury offering.
Otherwise, all the features combined would have been $25,000. The Luxe Package includes the complete FSD suite, lifetime premium connectivity, lifetime free supercharging, windshield protection plan, and wheel and tire protection plan, along with a four-year recommended maintenance plan.
The owner didn’t benefit from these perks much, as he sold his brand-new Tesla Model X after just eight months of ownership and 10,954 miles (17,629 kilometers). That is how far he traveled with his Tesla with a tri-motor setup. The system pushes out 1,020 horsepower (1,034 metric horsepower) and 752 pound-feet (1,020 Newton meters) of torque.
Photo: Cars and Bids Those are enough to make it rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 2.5 seconds with the one-foot rollout subtracted, run the quarter mile in 9.9 seconds with a trap speed of 144 mph (232 kph), and max out at 149 mph (240 kph). A 100-kWh liquid-cooled lithium-ion battery pack (95 kWh usable) stores enough energy for a drive of up to 326 miles (525 kilometers) before the car needs to be plugged in again.
The listing doesn't provide any image of the window sticker, so there is no information about how much the original owner paid for the 2026 Tesla Model X Plaid with the Luxe Package , which would normally be around $160,000. What we do know is that he sold it for $137,000.
The six-seat still-new EV is now going to a new home with a clean Carfax report, a windshield and windshield wipers replaced, two key cards, a mobile charger connector, a tow hitch, a rear cargo net, and wheel covers.
Once he switches back to the Ford F-150 Lightning, he won't get the six seats or the neck-snapping performance, but the electric truck is by no means a slouch. The dual-motor powertrain pumps out 452 horsepower (458 metric horsepower) and 775 pound-feet (1,050 Newton meters) of torque.
Photo: Cars and Bids The truck does 0 to 60 in 4.0 seconds, flashes down the quarter mile in 12.4 seconds with a trap speed of 107 mph (172 kph) and tops out at 110 mph (177 kph). Sure, the Lightning isn't exactly lightning fast when you compare it to the Tesla Model X Plaid , but it’s got more space on board, it's got a cargo bed, and it's got the ground clearance and capabilities that the Model X can only dream of once it leaves the road behind.
And he surely won't get that much mileage on a single charge. The Standard Range battery pack with a capacity of 98 kWh is EPA-rated at 240 miles (390 kilometers), while the Extended-Range battery pack is good for a drive of up to 320 miles (515 kilometers).
Ford had run out of brand-new F-150 Lightnings . The final electric truck rolled off the production line in December 2025. So the only way for the former Model X Plaid owner to get one is, of course, the used car market. He should be fine with a budget of roughly $70,000.

Having linked its glucagon/GLP-1 candidate to a significant reduction in heavy drinking days, Altimmune is preparing to speak to the FDA in December about the design of a Phase 3 program.
Altimmune is gearing up to talk to the FDA next month about a pivotal program for its glucagon/GLP-1 dual receptor agonist pemvidutide, which reduced drinking in patients with alcohol use disorder in a mid-stage study.
The biotech, which shared topline results from the Phase 2 RECLAIM trial in July, provided another look at the data Monday at a meeting of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) in Denver. Investigators randomized about 100 people with alcohol use disorder (AUD) to receive pemvidutide or placebo once weekly for 24 weeks, together with a standardized behavioral intervention.
GLP-1
Altimmune rises as GLP-1/glucagon drug curbs heavy drinking in mid-stage study
Pemvidutide showed a “highly statistically significant” treatment effect in patients with alcohol use disorder. Altimmune is going up against Eli Lilly and newcomer Baseline Therapeutics, among others, in this space.
July 28, 2026
·
3 min read
·
Tristan Manalac
Read more
As reported in July, the trial met its primary endpoint. Compared to baseline, patients on pemvidutide had 4.2 fewer heavy-drinking days per week during weeks 21 to 24 of the trial. Patients on placebo had 2.75 fewer heavy-drinking days per week. The result was “highly statistically significant,” Altimmune said in July.
Now, Altimmune has scheduled an end-of-Phase 2 meeting with the FDA for next month to discuss the design of the Phase 3 registrational program for AUD.
In a note to investors, William Blair analysts named the 38% reduction in serum phosphatidylethanol (PEth)— a direct biomarker for alcohol consumption—versus a 5.9% increase with placebo, as the “strongest validation for pemvidutide in this indication.” Altimmune first disclosed the serum PEth data in its July release of topline results.
Noting the limitations of cross-trial comparisons, “pemvidutide appears to exhibit a more robust clinical profile than short-duration low-dose semaglutide,” the analysts said. A Phase 2 trial in February 2025 found weekly heavy-drinking days fell from two to less than one in 48 patients who took semaglutide, the GLP-1 receptor agonist that Novo sells as Ozempic and Wegovy, for nine weeks.
The potential benefits of GLP-1s in AUD have long intrigued biopharma.
Last year, Eli Lilly started two Phase 3 trials of brenipatide in adults with AUD. Lilly designed each trial to enroll 1,100 patients with AUD to assess whether taking brenipatide, a GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist, for 56 weeks changes drinking patterns. The studies are scheduled to wrap in early 2028, according to the federal trial database.
Noting the size and duration of the Lilly studies, William Blair said, “We believe Altimmune will require additional capital to fund a pivotal program in AUD.” Altimmune ended June with $519 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments. The biotech recently began a Phase 3 trial of pemvidutide in the liver disease metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH).
While the analysts believe pemvidutide has shown therapeutic activity in MASH, they have doubts about whether the Phase 2b data demonstrate clear clinical differentiation. As they noted, the MASH market is increasingly competitive, with Madrigal Pharmaceuticals’ Rezdiffra and Novo’s Wegovy already out there, and Boehringer Ingelheim and Lilly advancing assets through the clinic.

Lilly presents early data supporting GLP-1/GIP candidate’s potential in depression, alcohol use disorder
With a trillion-dollar market cap and a wildly successful GLP-1 portfolio, Eli Lilly isn’t resting on its laurels. At the Psych Congress 2026, the company presented early-stage data that could support the potential of its next-gen GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonist to treat diseases far beyond obesity.

KM Mazda CX-5 Reveals the Less Attractive Side of Cost-Cutting
9 photos
Photo: Mazda
In a bid to improve production costs while minimizing production complexity, Mazda found several ways to make this generation of the CX-5 less expensive to build than its predecessor. Introduced in 2025 for model year 2026, the KM generation of the compact-sized crossover also happens to be hindered by noticeable compromises inside the cabin.
Replacing softer materials with less expensive plastics is one of those compromises, and who could forget that Mazda also moved key functions previously handled by physical controls into the central touchscreen?
These changes sit alongside a cost-effective manufacturing strategy that involves two companies, namely Yazaki and Nippon Steel.
First reported by Automotive News, the factory-side improvements are designed to improve profitability without losing the Japanese manufacturer's ability to compete in a segment where competitive pricing remains a touchy subject due to newcomers from China.
By involving suppliers much earlier in the development of the third-generation CX-5, the automaker enabled those suppliers to influence the engineering before the design became too expensive to change.
Yazaki, which is one of the world's largest wire harness manufacturers by yearly sales volumes, managed to reduce the number of wiring harness variants by 80 percent compared to the second-generation CX-5. Internally referred to as KF, the preceding design was produced for model years 2017 through 2025.
The 80 percent reduction comes from changing the manufacturing process itself. Yazaki and Mazda started work in 2022, reviewing all wiring configurations and production requirements with automation in mind.
Rather than designing complicated electrical assemblies and subsequently asking suppliers to figure out how to manufacture those harnesses efficiently, this relationship focused on simplifying both components and production methods together.
Photo: Mazda Clever in hindsight, for sure, but it takes vision to actually make it happen. The new arrangement brings wire harness production closer to Mazda's vehicle assembly operations, improving logistics in the process.
Nippon Steel, meanwhile, helped Mazda develop a stronger vehicle platform that allowed the Hiroshima-based manufacturer to reduce body weight by 10 percent compared to previous methods. What previous methods, Automotive News does not mention.
A quick search using your preferred search engine reveals a pretty drastic weight difference between the 2025 and 2026 models. In the US market, the 2.5 S AWD grade used to weigh 3,679 pounds (1,669 kilograms) compared to 3,856 pounds (1,749 kilograms) for the current generation. Truth be told, the KM offers considerably more standard tech, active safety features, and interior space.
Gifted with a longer overall length and a 4.6-inch longer wheelbase, the 2026 and newer models are somewhat underwhelming when you actually get behind the wheel. The redesigned dashboard may look contemporary due to a clear focus on minimalism, but hard plastics and fewer soft-touch surfaces clearly indicate a poorly executed cost-cutting effort.
Cabin appearance should never be confused with material quality. Removing some of the tactile quality that previously distinguished Mazda in the segment goes beyond these minor complaints. PARIS — France ordered two military Earth-observation satellites from Airbus and Thales Alenia Space for more than €1.5 billion (US$1.7 billion) to replace three existing orbiters, and to maintain a space-based image-intelligence capability beyond 2035.
The new satellites in the IRIS system will have an improved operational performance in terms of quality and the speed of making images available compared to the current CSO satellites, France’s Directorate General of Armament said on Monday . They’ll be able to take extremely high resolution images day and night in both the visible and the infrared spectrum around the world, the DGA said.
France is one of the few European NATO members with a sovereign constellation of high-end optical spy satellites, with many allies relying on lower-resolution assets and intelligence supplied by the United States. French President Emmanuel Macron said in January that France was providing two thirds of the intelligence capabilities supplied to Ukraine.
“The IRIS program aims to ensure the continuity of this capability while improving performance to meet the needs of the forces in a rapidly evolving strategic environment,” the DGA said.
The contract represents a value of more than €1.5 billion for the entire consortium, Airbus said in a separate statement . Airbus said it will provide the satellite platforms, a “significant share” of the payload on the first satellite and be responsible for the ground segment, while Thales Alenia Space will develop the second payload, provide critical elements of the first and contribute to the ground segment.
The new system, called IRIS after the French abbreviation of Instruments for Space Intelligence and Imaging, will be operated by the Space Command within the French Air and Space Force, though the DGA said the program is “resolutely open to cooperation” to allow partner countries to access the system.
The first of the new satellites is planned to become operational in 2033, with both in orbit around 2035, according to the DGA. The three satellites in the existing CSO system, for Composante Spatiale Optique, were launched in 2018, 2020 and 2025, respectively.
The DGA said it notified Airbus Defence and Space and Thales Alenia Space of the satellite order on Nov. 5. Subcontractors include Lynred, Pyxalis, Sodern, Safran Reosc and Air Liquide Advanced Technologies, according to the DGA.
The first IRIS satellite will replace the existing CSO-1 and CSO-2 satellites to ensure continuity of France’s space-based imagery intelligence capability, Thales said in a separate statement . After the end of the operational life of the last CSO satellite, the second IRIS satellite will “significantly enhance” image-resolution performance, it said.
Technologies developed for the IRIS system include a “hyper-stable” telescope with active optics, ultra-sensitive high-speed digital sensors and AI-based image processing, according to Thales, which owns 67% of Thales Alenia Space, with the remainder held by Italy’s Leonardo.
IRIS will integrate “the most advanced optical instrument ever built in Europe,” Thales Alenia Space CEO Hervé Derrey said in the statement.

Diesel-electric locomotives have been barreling along America’s wide-open spaces for generations, and the century-old combination of highly efficient diesel engines spinning up generators to power high-torque electric motors has proven tough to beat. Now, Caterpillar is putting that century-old concept to work underground. Meet the CAT R3200 XE LHD.
One of the many hard-working machines moving chunks of Earth under your feet, an LHD (load, haul, and dump) machine is essentially a massive underground wheel loader designed to scoop up blasted rock, haul it through narrow mine tunnels, then dump it into trucks or ore passes . Built low and wide to fit in the tunnels, LHDs are workhorses of underground mining operations – and the new R3200 XE is CAT’s biggest yet, with a 25 ton payload and electric drive.
Before we get into the machine’s specs (the few that we have, anyway), I want to make sure understand that large-scale mining operations use obscene amounts of fuel, and a swing in site efficiency of just 1-2% can mean a huge difference in the bottom line – and fuel prices were up 27.4% (!) in August alone .
Keep the staggering weight of what that kind of fuel cost can mean to a fleet that buys fuel by the literal truckload as you read the rest of this.

Though not yet officially released by CAT, snippets of the company’s launch video have been leaking through dealers and trade journals , and they show the big machine powered by CAT’s newest 18.1 liter Tier 5 C18 diesel generator making 527 hp (~390 kW). That C18 reportedly sends electrons to the same electric drive system used in the company’s already successful 18-ton R2900 XE LHD.
In addition to a bigger generator and heftier payload, CAT says the upcoming R3200 XE LHD offers reduced cycle times versus the R2900 XE with 11% better speed on grade, plus reduced maintenance and repair costs thanks to design refinements for better durability, including redesigned axle. All told, that works out to 28% more tons per hour with 8% better fuel efficiency.
That efficiency is boosted by the same baked-in ADAS tech that’s made the smaller R2900 XE a favorite, and includes the latest version of CAT AutoDig and MineStar, ensuring that the machines are easy for experienced CAT operators to set up for remote, semi-autonomous, and even fully autonomous operation using Command for Underground .

We have been patiently waiting over the course of many weeks for the good folks over at the racing-focused ' Import 2 Race ' channel on YouTube to come back home to their traditional venue - Island Dragway in Great Meadows, New Jersey.
That still hasn’t happened, and there’s still no sign of seeing them home any time soon to check out new quarter-mile dragstrip skirmishes. Instead, they found a massive passion for the lesser-known sport of roll races – initially, we have been treated to a series of 65-mph roll race battles, with all the high-speed action taking place at the iconic Pocono Raceway , a 2.5-mile tri-oval track in Blakeslee, Pennsylvania.
Later on, the videographer did make a change of scenery, though not also of the racing format. As such, while they’re still not back at Island Dragway, they are at least inching closer, and have shown us a new series of 45-mph roll races from the 2026 Sunday Funday Mod2Fame event . The action took place at an airport in Sullivan County, New York, with the format being the 45-mph roll race variety because, obviously, their strip isn’t as long as the massive straight at Pocono.
There’s no scoreboard either, so we have to rely on the rather unreliable natural eyesight, and such there’s also no way of knowing the actual roll speeds. At least the protagonists are feisty: we have seen the S650 Ford Mustang Dark Horse, the C8 iteration of the Chevrolet Corvette ZR1, the Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 from the S550 series, tuned ‘Vettes, and even older stuff like the Cadillac CTS-V.
Now, the latest skirmish involves a white and black-accented S550 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 rocking the mighty Predator 5.2-liter supercharged V8 as it goes up against a blue Chevrolet Corvette Z06 of the C7 variety, thus packing the traditional front-engine V8 and RWD. This was an interesting skirmish, of course, featuring archrivals that go for different values when it comes to the sports car phenomenon – the raw, brute force of the Shelby clashes with the elegant power delivery of the nimbler C7 Corvette.
Anyway, there is only one possible outcome – someone is going home victorious. Both sports cars looked composed as they prepared to unleash their roaring V8s, and once they floored the accelerator pedal, it was pretty clear that on the unprepped tarmac, all bets are off. In the end, we didn’t need a photo finish despite the admirable efforts of the underdog.
So, the Shelby GT500 reconfirmed its status and narrowly beat the pursuing Z06, which was close – but not close enough. Of course, in the present, the status of liberties and the balance of power might be a little different, but we’ll have to wait and see if anyone catches a skirmish between the newer Dark Horse SC and the C8 Corvette Z06.

14 photos
Photo: Tesla
An autonomous taxi should have one simple job beyond getting its passenger to the desired destination, and that is to stop when the passenger asks it to. The Cybercab apparently struggled with that part of the assignment when Jeremy Clarkson of Top Gear and Grand Tour experienced the driverless Tesla.
His Austin experience involved a failed pickup, a Cybercab that ignored Clarkson's inputted destination, and a particularly agonizing period when Jeremy could not persuade the car to stop or even open its doors. Had it been a medical emergency, this kind of shortfall would have been completely unacceptable.
JC recounted the Cybercab experience in his latest column for The Sunday Times, offering a less enthusiastic account of Tesla's design and self-driving software than what you might have seen from social media influencers who like to praise Elon Musk for just about everything, including the bad parts of his personality.
Getting inside the Cybercab proved troublesome for Clarkson. He watched the vehicle approach his pickup location through the app, only for the Cybercab in question to stop around the corner. Imagine this error happening during a torrential downpour. After climbing aboard, the Cybercab remained stationary while its digital assistant insisted that it was already heading toward the destination.
As fate would have it, a human representative eventually intervened, speaking through the car's audio system. The Tesla representative explained to Clarkson that he must cancel the booking and summon another vehicle, adding to his frustration. The replacement Cybercab navigated traffic smoothly enough, and JC humorously tested its conversational abilities during the ride by talking about the Tottenham Hotspur football club.
Photo: Tesla The replacement Cybercab, however, fumbled Clarkson once it had reached the destination. Not only did it continue driving, but the auto-driving vehicle announced that it needed to find somewhere else safe enough to pull over. Jeremy claims the car had already passed several places that looked perfectly suitable.
During this process, Clarkson noticed a few glitches in the central display that represented surrounding traffic. Phantom braking and an awkward encounter with an autonomous shopping trolley are further mentioned, and worse still, the car "seemingly" went through some red lights. "Seemingly" does the heavy lifting here, but nevertheless, running a red light is unacceptable auto-driving behavior.
Last but not least, Clarkson's account includes multiple ignored requests to stop and open the doors. JC admitted that said experience unsettled him, acknowledging that he could not do anything meaningful to resolve the aforementioned issues. The problem here is that Tesla removes the steering wheel and the pedal box, a perfectly understandable decision for a machine that never expects a human to take over.
Manual controls are welcomed in situations that cannot be resolved by software alone. As it stands, the Cybercab passenger depends on the vehicle's software recognizing the problem and accepting the instruction to stop. Given the British lad's experience, how are you guys feeling about Tesla intending to launch customer deliveries before year's end?
If you ask me, that would be a big fat no. As long as the Cybercab runs red lights, imagines things in front of it, and overlooks a passenger's instruction to stop, the software definitely needs polishing.

By Angelo Mathais India correspondent
10 November 2026
Indian trades are seeing a fresh wave of container capacity injections by Asian carriers, as regional freight demand remains upbeat.
Among the predominant regional lines, OOCL, HMM, and Emirates Shipping (ESL) have markedly consolidated their operations in India in recent months, with more service launches and network enhancements.
Hong Kong-based OOCL is to launch a shuttle loop connecting India’s east coast ports of Chennai and Visakhapatnam to Port Klang in Malaysia at the end of the month, a single port of destination (POD) connection targeting Indian transhipment cargo.
“The FCS4 will provide direct connections, offering improved flexibility, connectivity, and service reliability for cargo movements between Malaysia and East India,” the Cosco subsidiary told customers.
The move complements two intra-Asia services OOCL added out of India’s west coast (JNPA/Mundra) in Q2 26. They are: South-east Asia–Indian Subcontinent Service 2 (SIS2), on a rotation of Qinzhou, Yangpu, Haiphong, Singapore, Mundra, Singapore, Hong Kong and Qinzhou; and the South-east Asia–Indian Subcontinent Service (SIS), rotating Laem Chabang, Singapore, Port Klang, JNPA (Nhava Sheva), Mundra, Karachi, Port Klang, Singapore and Laem Chabang.
Similarly, ESL has expanded its capacity out of India by splitting its Red Sea network into two loops, deploying two vessels on each in a pendulum fashion. The upgraded twin operations begin this month: the South Red Sea Service (SRS), on a rotation of JNPA, Jeddah, and JNPA; and the North Red Sea Service (NRS), on a rotation of JNPA, Djibouti, Aqaba, Sokhna, Sohar, and JNPA, according to industry updates.
Meanwhile, South Korean liner HMM opened a new India-East Africa loop in late September, in conjunction with Cosco, Interasia Lines, and PIL, to tap into growing demand on the trade. The Gulf–India–East Africa (GIA) links JNPA, Mundra, Dar es Salaam, Mombasa, and JNPA on a 35-day rotation, arguably a more competitive option than other networks previously available for the promising India-Africa market.
Alongside the entrenched operators, Indian shippers have seen capacity coming from new market entrants, like Vietnam-based Hai An Lines, which last month launched the standalone CVI service connecting Chennai, South-east Asia and China, with the 1,800-teu Haian Beta .
Industry sources believe this frenzied capacity influx reflects carrier expectations of sustained growth opportunities ex-India, as the economy is forecast to expand faster than other traditional emerging markets. Its real GDP is estimated to have recorded an impressive 7.8% expansion in Q1 of fiscal year 2026-27, according to the latest government data.
Reflecting that buoyant economic outlook, container volumes through Indian ports, especially JNPA, have gained measurable pace this year. JNPA hit its highest-ever monthly throughput last month, handling some 865,000 teu, up from 680,000 teu in October 2025, with year-to-date volumes reaching 5.5m teu, a 19% spike year on year, data shows.
Despite the geopolitical challenges, India’s export sector has remained resilient through 2026, industry participants also claim.
“Our exporters continue to respond to uncertainty with agility, strengthening their presence across markets and product categories,” said SC Ralhan, president of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations.
“The broad-based contribution of traditional and emerging sectors adds depth to this performance,” he added.

By Charlotte Goldstone
10 November 2026
The global containership fleet is set to expand by almost 50% by 2030, with even record levels of vessel scrapping unlikely to prevent a severe supply imbalance.
In its latest report, Sea-Intelligence forecast the fleet will grow from almost 34m teu today to 40m teu by Q2 28, and 50m teu by the Q3 30.
The analyst expects average annual fleet growth of 10% between 2027 and 2030, based on existing orders, with further newbuilding contracts potentially increasing that figure.
Quarterly deliveries are forecast to average 1m teu over the period, peaking at 1.8m teu in the third quarter of 2028.
This compares with average quarterly deliveries of 560,000 teu between 2023 and 2026, highlighting the scale of capacity due to enter the market.
Sea-Intelligence said the current orderbook, covering vessels scheduled for delivery through March 2031, stood at 15.7m teu, equivalent to 46.4% of the existing fleet, while Xeneta’s latest assessment puts it slightly lower, at 15.47m teu – a difference of around 230,000 teu.
Sea-Intelligence said the ordering surge had begun in the third quarter of 2024, with new contracts averaging 1.5m teu every quarter.
So even an unprecedented demolition programme would do little to offset the incoming capacity, according to Sea-Intelligence. In 2016, carriers scrapped a record 670,000 teu, equivalent to just 3.3% of the fleet, during the industry’s previous overcapacity crisis.
Repeating that level of demolition every year between 2027 and 2030 would offset less than 17% of the scheduled deliveries, leaving annual fleet growth at 8.5%. Peter Sand, chief analyst at Xeneta, told The Loadstar only 600,000 teu had been demolished since 2019.
Xeneta estimates that just 3.4m teu of existing capacity is at least 21.8 years old, the average demolition age recorded between 2016 and 2019.
Mr Sand explained: “Containerships are built to last a life at sea, so they are mainly demolished for commercial and operational reasons rather than wear and tear.”
He expects demolition to increase if a large-scale return to Red Sea transits released capacity currently absorbed by longer voyages.
However, the age and size of vessels available for demolition complicate the prospect of meaningful fleet renewal.
Jonathan Roach, analyst at Braemar, told The Loadstar there were 1,944 vessels aged 20 years or more, with 1,903 ships on order. He said: “On paper, the numbers look remarkably similar, but this is where the comparison ends. There is a major mismatch in vessel sizes.”
Older vessels are concentrated in the smaller sub-panamax fleet, while newbuilding orders are weighted towards larger ships, he explained. This means demolition could remove substantial numbers of older vessels, but not compensating for an equivalent amount of incoming capacity.
Jan Tiedemann, VP liner strategy at Alphaliner, told The Loadstar he expected scrapping to increase in 2027 and 2028 without offsetting the newbuilding influx.
He identified several factors that could increase demand for vessel capacity, including longer trade routes, slow-steaming and rising consumption in emerging markets.

By Alex Lennane
10 November 2026
Freightos has launched a new AI-native platform for freight forwarders, as an increasingly bitter dispute between its management and founder Zvi Schreiber over the company’s growth strategy heads towards a shareholder showdown next month.
Dr Schreiber, who founded Freightos in 2012 and resigned from its board in February, has accused the company of abandoning its growth ambitions in favour of profitability, and is campaigning to remove chairman Udo Lange and change the company’s strategic direction.
“The board calls my plan a ‘sudden strategic pivot’. The opposite is true,” he told The Loadstar .
“For 14 years, Freightos’ strategy was to maximise growth, with the transactional platform as the primary long-term opportunity. That’s what shareholders invested in.”
But chief executive Pablo Pinillos rejected the suggestion that Freightos had to choose between expanding its transaction platform and developing its software business.
“There is not a real platform-first versus solutions-first idea, because in the end the platform and the solutions reinforce each other,” he told The Loadstar .
He argued that improved software, AI-driven decision-making, and automation would generate more bookings, producing additional data that would further improve the platform.
“Bookings follow,” he said, describing a strategy built around three interconnected layers: intelligence; orchestration; and network connectivity.
The new Freightos for Forwarders platform brings together carrier rates, quoting, procurement, booking management, and market intelligence, alongside AI agents designed to convert unstructured customer enquiries into quotations, using forwarders’ own commercial rules and margins.
Freightos said more than 300 forwarders were already operating on the new platform, although the AI modules and more advanced workflows were still being introduced progressively as customers migrated to the new system.
The refreshed interface and live booking functions are operational for migrated customers, with further AI capabilities, integrations, and tailored workflows to follow.
The company said it was aiming to reduce quotation turnaround times from hours or days to minutes, and improve quote-to-book conversion rates, but declined to provide projections for additional transactions generated by the launch.
The platform connects with more than 75 carriers and the 7LFreight trucking network, while APIs allow forwarders to integrate Freightos’s capabilities with existing transport management systems and proprietary AI tools.
Mr Pinillos said the upgraded technology should help drive growth in both software revenue and transaction volumes.
“The expectation is that we are able to get more volumes from a transactions perspective,” he said, while making Freightos’s software more embedded in customers’ operations.
But Dr Schreiber argues that the company has lost momentum by shifting its focus away from the neutral booking network that he believes represents its principal long-term opportunity.
In the second quarter, Freightos reported revenue of $7.7m, up just 3% year on year. Platform revenue increased 19%, to $2.9m, while Solutions revenue fell 4%, to $4.8m.
Dr Schreiber believes AI will increasingly commoditise software products, making the company’s carrier connectivity, transaction infrastructure, and marketplace network more valuable.
He wants Freightos to accelerate investment in its platform and relaunch its marketplace for small and medium-sized shippers.
Mr Pinillos said Freightos would continue developing its shipper products, including its enterprise-focused Procure offering and marketplace for smaller customers, although he gave no timetable for a comparable AI-native launch.
He also insisted that the company’s push towards profitability was not incompatible with renewed growth.
“Breakeven is not a strategy, and it’s not the finish line,” he said.
He described the breakeven target as a commitment made by previous management, in 2023, arguing that the company had needed greater discipline over investment returns and a cost base that had become too large for its near-term economics.
Achieving breakeven would allow Freightos to fund future growth from its own resources, he said.
But Dr Schreiber disputes the suggestion that more aggressive investment would require additional fundraising. He argued: “Freightos doesn’t need to raise money to grow. It already raised the capital for growth: that’s exactly why we went public, and what shareholders invested in.”
He said Freightos had approximately $21m in net cash and no debt, and needed to redirect its spending towards growing the transaction platform.
“Without aggressive platform growth, where is the upside for shareholders?” he asked.
Mr Pinillos said he expected double-digit revenue growth in the future, although the company would provide specific guidance separately.
The dispute is now heading towards a confrontation at Freightos’s annual general meeting on 16 December, where Dr Schreiber is seeking the removal of chairman Udo Lange, annual director elections, and an advisory resolution advocating changes to the company’s strategy.
“The Freightos board is now so anti-growth that it is engaging in what I can only call blatant vote rigging,” Dr Schreiber alleged.
He claims the company has effectively prevented shareholders from supporting his advisory resolution through its normal proxy voting arrangements, leaving attendance at the AGM as the only route to voting in favour.
“A shareholder who votes through their broker to remove the chairman, or simply to reappoint EY as auditors, will be recorded as voting against growth,” he said.
The company’s proxy statement confirms that Proposal 4, Dr Schreiber’s advisory resolution on strategy, has been omitted from its proxy card. It states that even shareholders who submit voting instructions on other resolutions will have their shares voted against Proposal 4.
Freightos said the decision followed legal advice, with the board arguing that the resolution was inconsistent with shareholders’ rights under applicable law and the company’s articles. It objected particularly to the proposal’s abstract wording and its combination of questions about chairman qualifications and corporate strategy.
Asked whether shareholders could support the resolution without travelling to Israel, Mr Pinillos told The Loadstar that they would need to attend the AGM, although he suggested online attendance might be possible.
“It could be online or could be physically,” he said, adding that the company had not yet decided how attendance would be defined for the meeting.
Mr Pinillos also defended the board’s opposition to annual director elections, arguing that the existing staggered structure provided continuity, and that annual elections risked introducing instability into the company’s long-term strategy.
Asked about departures from Freightos’ management team, he acknowledged that parts of the organisation, including management, needed rebuilding.
However, he declined to engage directly with Dr Schreiber’s criticism of the board.
“I don’t have anything more than respect for what he has built in this company,” he said. “I’m not focused on who is right or who is wrong.”
At the conclusion of the interview, he added: “What I’m not willing to spend a single second of my time on is debating someone else’s opinions.”
With Freightos now rolling out its next generation of AI-enabled technology, the question is whether its integrated approach can deliver the renewed growth both sides say they want, without the change of strategy and leadership demanded by its founder.

By Alex Lennane
10 November 2026
International belly-cargo operations at Shenzhen will be suspended during next week’s APEC summit, while sharply reduced freighter slots threaten to divert peak-season shipments into neighbouring airports.
The restrictions affect imports and exports through mainland China’s third-largest cargo airport, with forwarders warning of tighter space, congestion and higher rates at alternative gateways. Elsewhere in the region, Taiwan’s cargo congestion is expected to delay freighter operations throughout Q4.
The APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting takes place in Shenzhen on 18–19 November. The international belly-cargo suspension runs from midnight on 16 November until 6pm on 20 November, local time.
“All international passenger flights inbound/outbound SZX are prohibited from carrying belly cargo within this window. No belly shipment can be accepted,” Kathy Liu, VP sales & marketing for Dimerco, told The Loadstar .
The confirmation reinforces a published notice from Teleport, which instructs cargo agents and terminal operators not to accept or handle cargo for affected passenger services.
Freighter operations will face substantial restrictions, although a blanket shutdown has not been announced.
“There is NO official full suspension of all freighter flights,” said Ms Liu. However, slots would be “drastically reduced”, with earlier cargo cutoffs and selective acceptance by carriers. Some could temporarily suspend collection services, while dangerous goods, perishables and priority shipments were highly likely to be refused.
International passenger services would generally remain available, although schedules could change and some flights could be cancelled to accommodate traffic priorities, she added.
ANA Cargo’s notice, issued yesterday, restricts dangerous goods through 20 November, including excepted quantities and goods normally treated as unrestricted under special provisions. Previously booked dangerous goods shipments travelling 9-15 November can still be accepted, but new bookings are barred.
From 16-20 November, ANA will also refuse perishables, PRIO products, time-sensitive shipments, cargo exceeding its AKE container-door dimensions, and shipper-built units, other than those using AKE containers.
The restrictions cover arrivals, departures, and air-to-air connections through Shenzhen. Air-to-road connections are exempt from the transit provision.
For accepted shipments, ANA requires exports to be tendered at least 12 hours before scheduled departure, while imports will become available for collection at least eight hours after arrival. The carrier attributes the measures to instructions from local authorities ahead of APEC.
Teleport has published a broader notice, saying international passenger flights arriving at or departing from Shenzhen will be prohibited from carrying cargo between midnight on 16 November and 6pm on 20 November, local time. Its advisory instructs cargo agents and terminal operators not to accept or handle cargo for affected services.
The published notices differ in scope, and an airport-wide embargo covering all operators has not been independently established.
UPS, meanwhile, has announced temporary adjustments to import, export, collection, and delivery services in selected areas from 12-21 November, citing traffic controls and enhanced security screening.
Road restrictions will add another constraint. Shenzhen police have banned dangerous-goods vehicles from all city roads, including expressways, on 16–20 November. Other freight vehicles face restrictions on specified roads and in selected districts at different times.
The city’s Ports Office has also urged cross-border freight companies to bring stock movements forward, postpone non-urgent orders, and stagger necessary journeys during the summit week.
Dimerco warned in its 3 November freight report that APEC “may halt Shenzhen terminal acceptance on 16–20 November”, advising customers to plan South China exports around restrictions. The forwarder also identified APEC and winter schedule changes as constraints on freighter and belly capacity during the year-end peak.
Hong Kong and Guangzhou offer alternative gateways, but securing uplift could prove difficult. Geodis has recommended considering both airports, while Zencargo warned that Shenzhen flight cancellations would divert cargo into Guangzhou, leaving “very tight space” on services to Europe and the US.
The disruption comes as peak season demand pushes up China’s airfreight rates.
Freightos reported today that China-US prices increased 3% last week to more than $8/kg, already reaching the previous year’s high, recorded only in mid-December. China–Europe rates rose 11%, to $4.87,/kg, up 23% year on year.
Shenzhen handled approximately 2.05m tonnes of cargo and mail in 2025, including 1.06m tonnes of international and regional traffic.
The airport has developed specialist handling arrangements for lithium batteries, battery-containing electronics and vaping products, potentially exposing established export flows to dangerous goods restrictions. Its first-half report this year records the launch of bonded e-cigarette export operations.
Perishable imports are also exposed: Shenzhen handled 25,000 tonnes of fresh and cold-chain imports in the first half of 2026, up 37.1% year on year. The total tonnage covered by the announced restrictions has not been established.
Meanwhile, congestion at Taiwan Taoyuan Airport is expected to delay freighter operations throughout Q4, extending the disruption previously reported by The Loadstar .
In an update yesterday, Expeditors said ground handlers were serving 80-90 additional freighters a month above regular commercial flights. Exports of AI servers and semiconductor equipment, alongside imports of equipment, raw materials, and server parts, were stretching resources.
Imports awaiting breakdown had occupied cargo dollies needed to move exports to the ramp. Dolly availability has improved, but staffing constraints and the residual backlog mean recovery remains gradual.
China Airlines’ freighter services have experienced the most disruption. Expeditors said “freighter delays are expected throughout Q4”, although it did not expect large-scale cancellations to continue.
Further cancellations remain possible as handlers clear the backlog, with longer handling times, delayed import availability, and onward connections remaining concerns.

Blue Origin Shows Off the Northstar, A Simpler and More Powerful Rocket Engine Than the BE-4
6 photos
Photo: Blue Origin
On the same week in announced it has developed a third stage for the two-stage New Glenn rocket, American private space company Blue Origin made public the initial details of its second rocket engine, something that will be known from now on as the Northstar.
The reusable booster powerplant burns liquid oxygen and liquefied natural gas (LOX/LNG) to produce a total power of 715,000 pounds of thrust with throttle capability. That's significantly more than the BE-4 the company currently uses on its rockets (that one is rated at 640,000 pounds of thrust), but that's not even the most important part.
Blue Origin says that the Northstar is 65 percent made through additive manufacturing, which not only makes it cheaper to produce, but also allows it to be assembled in less than a day. This approach also permitted the company to go from program approval to development testing in less than a year.
Although the new engine keeps the same staged combustion cycle as the BE-4, it is 30 percent lighter and at the same time uses 50 percent fewer parts.
Blue Origin does not say when its second booster engine will become operational, or on what version of the New Glenn rocket it will be fitted. Overall, the Northstar has now become the company's fifth engine.
The company entered the rocket engine-making industry with the BE-3PM, which came about as the first new liquid hydrogen-fueled rocket engine to be developed for production in the United States in over a decade.
It was used for the first time at the end of 2015, when it powered the New Shepard Propulsion Module just above the Karman line. Later on, in 2021, it was slapped on the same rocket to take Blue Origin's first paying customers to space.
It was used for a total of 38 missions and, when the company pulled the plug on its New Shepard commercial spaceflight program, the number of people that reached space thanks to this engine had risen to 98.
Over time, Blue Origin developed the BE-7 engine meant to power the company's lunar landers, specifically the Blue Moon . Then, the BE-3U is meant for the second stage of the New Glenn rocket, in both the 7x2 and the 9x4 configurations, which translate into two of them for the former and four of them for the latter.
Last but not least, the BE-4 is the engine fitted at the bottom of the New Glenn booster as the first oxygen-rich staged combustion engine made in the U.S., either seven of them or nine, depending on configuration. Additionally, two of them have been fitted on the first stage of United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket.
We will keep an eye on Blue Origin and report back once we know more about the new Northstar engine.

Sorry, but here's all the proof you need.
While this car isn't a delivery miles example, it's not particularly high-mileage either. It was driven only 6,600 miles since new, which points to it having been a weekend getaway car or a family vacation car. Still, it lost 38.15% of its original value in the blink of an eye. The owner basically paid almost $19 per mile to drive this car. This type of math hurts my brain. At this point, just get a G-Wagen, because it's the only SUV that's unusually resistant to depreciation.
Fine, you want something quicker than a G-Class, alright, no problem. How about the Urus Performante? It too will hold on to its original value a lot better than a DBX707.

UPS has its sights set on US Customs and Border Protection (CBP), launching legal action against the agency to reclaim refunds and interest for tariffs paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), with it having already received some $500m.
Filed at the US Court of International Trade on Friday, the lawsuit seeks to compel CBP to re-liquidate entries and issue refunds, not only for duties paid, but also accrued interest, after the US Supreme Court ruled the tariffs unlawful in February.
The lawsuit covers entries for which UPS was the ‘importer of record’ (IOR), allowing it to claim refunds directly from CBP, although the integrator noted that, in many cases, it was customers that had borne the cost of the duties. It said it would pass any recovered funds to them.
Together with UPS, United Parcel Service Oasis Supply Corp and UPS Supply Chain Solutions are seeking the re-liquidation of entries on which the ‘unlawful’ duties were assessed, including those that have already been finally liquidated.
Under the CBP’s phased Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries (CAPE), April’s Phase 1 covered unliquidated entries and certain entries liquidated within the previous 80 days, Phase 2 followed in June, with Phase 3 opening last month.
This covers finally liquidated entries, but refunds can only be processed where the importer has obtained an order for re-liquidation from the Court of International Trade – CBP maintains that such an order is required before it can repay the duties.
Pointing to previous assurances from the government that refunds, including interest, would be made if the IEEPA tariffs were found unlawful, UPS said its claim was intended to preserve its own and its customers’ rights to recover the money.
Having received some $500m from CBP under the tariff refund programme, UPS’s latest quarterly filings indicated that, by the start of October, it had passed on around $230m, with $270m still owed to customers.

This Bugatti Tourbillon Miniature Takes 300 Hours To Build and Costs 2027 Honda Civic Money
24 photos
Photo: Amalgam Collection
Spending $24,095 on a car in the United States of America gets you a base compact sedan. Amalgam Collection has a rather different interpretation of what that kind of money should buy, with the British specialist asking this much for each of its 1:8 scale Bugatti Tourbillon replicas. The miniature hypercars measure over 58 centimeters (23 inches) in length and feature the finest quality materials.
Each unit requires over 300 hours of assembly, and its dimensions alone mean that prospective customers might need to rearrange furniture in order to find somewhere suitable to display it. As of this writing, two versions of the scale model reproduce different factory specs of the V16 plug-in hybrid thriller.
Signature Specification leads the way, boasting the launch car's two-tone finish that combines Aerolithe and Aventurine. Only 199 units are in the offing. Equipe Pur Sang Specification is the other one, swapping the understated combo from earlier for Grigio paintwork and Italian Red accents. The Pur Sang recreates the actual vehicle Bugatti used to present said package back in March 2025.
Think of the Pur Sang as the most sporting Tourbillon available for the time being, although 'available' may not be the right word because every single Tourbillon has been spoken for. Additional design elements include a specific front splitter and a more audacious exhaust setup. This one is also limited to 199 examples.
All told, development work required more than 3,000 hours. Amalgam Collection offers bespoke commissions for customers who want their 1:8 scale models to match a particular specification, which means that Amalgam is actually targeting Tourbillon clients rather than average Joes and Janes with deep pockets.
Photo: Amalgam Collection The peeps at Amalgam tasked a small team of craftspeople to put together thousands of individual components, including castings, CNC-machined metal parts, and photo-etched details. More interestingly, the reference material comes from Bugatti's very own material specifications, paint codes, and computer-aided design files. The automaker's own designers and engineers helped Amalgam come up with both designs, ensuring complete accuracy of representation.
An unusually involved development process when you think about it, but hey, both Amalgam and Bugatti understand that attention to detail matters a lot. At this price, which is nearly enough to get you a brand-new Civic sedan for model year 2027, getting anything wrong would be a fairly expensive embarrassment.
On the road, the actual Tourbillon is the first-ever Bug developed with Mate Rimac at the helm. Capable of 1,800 ps (1,775 hp) at full chatter, the Chiron's replacement combines a naturally aspirated V16 developed and produced by Cosworth with no fewer than three electric drive units. Croatian electric hypercar specialist is credited with developing the high-voltage battery and the e-axles, along with the silicon-carbide inverters and torque-vectoring control software.
Tipping the scales at under two metric tons, Bugatti's newest design will be produced in 250 units. Built around a carbon-composite monocoque that integrates the plug-in hybrid battery as a structural element, this bad boy further boasts 3D-printed suspension components and e-actuated dihedral doors.
Flaunting an unashamedly mechanical instrument cluster mounted to a fixed-hub steering wheel, the Tourbillon also features an infotainment screen that can be hidden to clean up the dash. In optimal conditions, the Speed Key enables an electronically limited maximum speed of 276 miles per hour (445 kilometers per hour), making it faster than most Chirons. Only an unrestricted Super Sport 300+ can do better, namely 305 mph (490 kph) in controlled testing conditions.

Turtle Cottage Is a 41-ft Tiny Home With a Wooden Deck, Catpatio, and a Surprising Amount of Storage
20 photos
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot
Some people who decide to move into a tiny house prefer to place their new dwelling on private land and live independently, while others would rather have it parked in a tiny home community where they can enjoy shared gathering spaces and gardens to combat isolation.
More and more tiny home communities are popping up across the United States, often in quiet places that feel like true retreats. They represent an appealing alternative to traditional housing, especially for seniors who prefer to age in place, combining the benefits of minimalist living with the convenience of shared spaces and resources.
Kala’s tiny house on wheels is parked in one such community, allowing her to enjoy a simplified life with lower living expenses and a closer connection to nature. Kala’s compact home, which she calls the Turtle Cottage, is located in Tiny Tranquility, a community of more than 40 tiny houses on the Oregon coast, about two miles south of Waldport. It’s very close to the ocean, providing a dreamy coastal setting and the benefit of enjoying nature whenever she wants.
Built on a triple-axle gooseneck trailer, the tiny home is 41 feet (12.5 meters) long and 8.5 feet (2.6 meters) wide, and it was built by Mint Tiny House Company, a well-versed builder based in Vancouver that specializes in custom tiny house RVs, park models, and modern prefab modular homes. Kala purchased it from a previous owner for $145,000 and has been living there full-time with her two cats for the past year.
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot Finished in green-painted board-and-batten siding, Turtle Cottage fits perfectly into its surroundings. The main attraction on the outside is a spacious back wooden deck with a protective railing. She had it built by a local contractor, and it significantly extends her living space to the outside. It’s large enough to accommodate an outdoor seating arrangement, but the best thing about it is that it offers lovely views of the meadow and the surrounding trees.
The house also has a covered patio directly in front of the main entrance. It is enclosed with protective netting, and Kala turned it into a private catio - an outdoor space where her two cats can safely enjoy some fresh air.
Inside the Turtle Cottage, every nook and cranny serves a purpose, but the living space does not feel cramped or overwhelming. On the contrary, thanks to the glass door and an abundance of windows all the way up to the ceiling that flood the home with natural light, every area feels open and inviting . The white tongue-and-groove pine walls maintain the bright atmosphere, while the natural wood window frames and exposed beams add a tinge of rustic charm.
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot Given the generous length of the house, there is plenty of space inside for everything needed for full-time living, especially for a single person. The layout includes an open-plan kitchen and living area, a private bedroom over the gooseneck, a separate bathroom, and a large loft.
Centrally located, the kitchen is large and well-equipped. With both floor-based and overhead cabinets, it offers plenty of space for cooking essentials, and everything is cleverly arranged to ensure an easy workflow. Kala confesses cooking is really not her passion, but she has everything she needs for home-cooked meals, including an oven, a three-burner gas cooktop, and a microwave.
The kitchen is also equipped with a large farmhouse sink with a little drainer, a full-size refrigerator, and durable granite countertops.
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot The living room is not very large but feels snug and intimate, designed for comfort and relaxation. Kala furnished it with a comfortable two-person sofa, a side table, a TV stand with shelves and drawers, and a big cat tree, turning it into a comfortable space for both her and her pets. The high, vaulted ceiling in this area makes it feel a bit more spacious, and all the windows open for fresh air and ventilation.
From the kitchen, a staircase leads up to the loft and a narrow hallway takes you to the bathroom and gooseneck bedroom. The bathroom is located just under the loft, but the ceiling is still quite high, and the room is spacious and comfortable. What’s more, it is fitted with everything needed for full-time living, including a full-size shower with a glass door, a regular flushing toilet, a vanity sink, a washer/dryer machine, and even generous storage.
Four storage steps and a steel handrail make access to the bedroom really easy. The room has all the qualities of a proper bedroom, with full standing height, space to move around the comfortable double bed, a sliding door for privacy, and two massive windows flanking the bed. Drawers on all sides of the bed add a generous amount of extra storage for clothes and other belongings.
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot As mentioned, Kala’s tiny house also features a loft. It’s actually a very large loft that goes all the way to the front of the house. It can accommodate a mattress or a daybed if she ever wanted to have visitors, but right now, she only uses for storage. The loft is accessed through an L-shaped staircase whose functionality goes beyond just a point of access. Its stair treads lift up to reveal extra storage, and underneath it there is also a slide-out pantry and a coat cabinet.
Kala chose tiny living for the simplified lifestyle and closeness to nature, but it also brought her more financial freedom. For the parking spot in the tiny house community, she pays $872 per month, and that includes all the utilities and the use of the shared amenities.
